title: Continuous Vital Sign Monitoring Versus Routine Spot-checks in Patients After Non-cardiac Surgery
official: The Effect of Continuous Monitoring Versus Routine Spot-checks on Altered Vital Signs in Patients Recovering From Non-cardiac Surgery on Normal Wards: the "COME ON, NOW!" Trial
summary: The "COME ON, NOW!" trial is a randomized, single-center trial in patients recovering from non-cardiac surgery on normal wards investigating whether continuous vital sign monitoring - compared to routine spot-checks by nurses - reduces the total duration of abnormal vital signs per hour during the first 48 hours after admission to the normal ward.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Consenting patients ≥45 years scheduled for elective non-cardiac (abdominal and thoracic) surgery with planned postoperative admission to a normal ward after an overnight stay in an advanced post-anesthesia care unit.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Emergency surgery
* Pregnancy
* Impossibility to perform continuous monitoring with the Radius VSM sensor (Masimo, Irvine, CA)
* Atrial fibrillation
* Patients designated Do Not Resuscitate, or are receiving end-of-life care
